correctness.rationale: The discovery process is a sum of independent Bernoulli variables at every scaled time. The finite harmonic root is unique, its first two terms follow from a super-algebraically accurate infinite-kernel Euler--Maclaurin formula and an explicit finite truncation tail. The normalized mass variance tends to 1/2 and Lyapunov ratio tends to zero at rate O(a_n^{-1/2}). A local mean derivative of 1/a_n and monotone threshold inversion give the Gaussian hitting-time law. The offset B_n^{3/2}/n determines the sharp exponent boundary. The executable finite checker passes; these experiments are not substituted for proof.

The sharp 2/3 threshold specifies exactly when the natural explicit leading deterministic center ceases to give a properly centered Gaussian, with a nonzero endpoint shift. This is mathematically motivated by the sharpness of the source first-order limit, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
